correctness.rationale: For L<min(5,t+2), opposite complementary sides of the central t-square cannot both hold a full unit square because L-t<2. Reflect to one vertical strip and one horizontal strip. Each strip has width<2; any two assigned unit-square short-axis projections overlap interiorly, so long-axis unit intervals are disjoint and at most four per strip since L<5. Eight items force exactly four in each. The extreme rightmost horizontal-strip square and topmost vertical-strip square have long-axis lower coordinates at least 3, while t+1>L-1, giving strict overlap in both x and y, contradiction. For 2≤t≤3, 3≤t≤4, t≥4 the source supplies complete coordinate packings respectively in squares t+2,5,t+1. The single-unit separation gives t+1 lower bound at t≥4; boundary equality is attained. The proof handles arbitrary translations/strip-overlap assignments and uncountable real t, not just sampled values.
